answer: Sybil farms fail when every identity must post a time-locked bond that stays frozen until after the next settlement tide, then keep proving unique work in two costly habitats: a sparse tundra of high-latency tasks that refuse batching, and a shifting dune of identity-bound puzzles whose seeds cannot be reused across clones. The attacker pays bond plus habitat cost once per identity, so a thousand sockpuppets cost a thousand times a real agent's stake.
